messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened — Regional networking degradation in us-west-2c. Several ELB target groups reporting high Unhealthy counts and packet loss to instances. Auto-detected by health-check-scraper at 2026-03-15T08:12:01Z

maria (oncall): getting paged, reading the alert. seeing 5xx spike on API frontends in us-west-2. marking Sev2 for now, will escalate if customers are impacted broadly.

derek (sre): can someone post quick numbers from monitoring? p95 latency, error rate, and which ELBs?

maria (oncall): Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/api-prod?orgId=1 (paste) — API 5xx rate jumped 8x for us-west-2c instances, p95 latency doubled. ELB: prod-api-elb-usw2 reports ~30% unhealthy targets in 2c.

tim (eng-infra): routing logs show repeated connection resets from within 2c to the targets' NICs. traceroute from a healthy host in 2a to an affected instance in 2c:
```
traceroute to ip-10-0-45-12.ec2.internal (10.0.45.12), 30 hops max
 1 10.0.1.1 0.5 ms
 2 10.0.3.9 0.9 ms
 3 10.0.12.77 3.8 ms  <--- long tail, some *
 4 * * *
```

aly (support): seeing incoming customer tickets: ~15 reports saying the product fails to load for west coast customers, some report intermittent success. many are on paid plans. CC'ing lisa for impact.

lisa (product): thanks, aly. can we get a quick customer impact summary for legal/CS? which customers, percentage affected, and mitigation plan?

maria (oncall): quick summary: 12 customer accounts with requests hitting us-west-2, rough traffic impact ~6% of total API calls globally but concentrated (top 3 customers account for ~65% of that region's traffic). We'll post a fuller post-incident once stable.

derek (sre): initial hypothesis: noisy network path or hypervisor NIC issue in 2c causing packet loss and ELB health-check failures. Also seeing Route53 health check flaps for the same endpoints.

incident-bot: pd-bot alerted on-call shift change in 18m — maria will handoff to derek if this is still active after the rotation.

maria (oncall): I'm going to run targeted mitigation: 1) disable cross-zone stickiness on prod-api-elb-usw2 to encourage routing away from 2c. 2) deregister unhealthy targets in 2c to force failover to 2a/2b. 3) open support with AWS. Doing step 1 now.

tim (eng-infra): re: step 1 — changing ELB cross-zone settings may cause uneven traffic; prefer to force-deregister bad targets first. Command: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:tg:prod-api-usw2 --targets Id=i-0abcd1234` (do one at a time). confirm before running?

maria (oncall): running deregister script against the clearly failing instances now (removing 6 targets). logs: `deregistered 6/6 targets from prod-api-elb-usw2` — monitoring for error rate change.

derek (sre): good. also enabling additional instance-level health checks (nc -z) to double-check port connectivity. running `ssh jump-usw2a -- nc -vz 10.0.45.12 443`

incident-bot: AWS Support case opened #123456789 — engineer assigned, ETA 30-60m. Case notes: EC2 networking issues in us-west-2c affecting multiple instances, observed packet loss and route instability.

aly (support): prod dashboard shows errors falling slowly after deregister — 5xx rate down ~60% in the last 10m. tickets still trickling in. updating customer queue with interim ETA: 'partial degradation in us-west-2, working on failover', ETA 1h.

lisa (product): will notify top affected customers via email template A (include status page link). Please flag any accounts that had data writes in-flight that might need reconciliation.

maria (oncall): customers with persistent failures: acct-321, acct-998 — both on higher throughput. I requested session replay logs for acct-321 to check for any failed writes.

tim (eng-infra): Route53 checks: some weighted records for internal metrics endpoints still prefer 2c due to TTL; recommending immediate low-TTL update and weighted shift to 2a/2b for production entries to speed traffic steering. I can push TTL=30s to the relevant records.

derek (sre): going to add a temporary traffic policy to prefer healthy azs and enable cross-region failover for the next 2 hours. Steps: 1) update Route53 weight, 2) push ELB listener override to prioritize healthy target groups.

maria (oncall): note — taking a brief handoff to todays-night oncall in 12m — derek, can you take primary after my rotation? pd-bot will page you.

derek (sre): I'll take over. plan for next 30m: 1) monitor AWS case, 2) complete Route53 weight shift, 3) coordinate with infra for potential AZ evacuation (boot new instances in other AZs if needed).

incident-bot: pd-bot has acknowledged handoff to derek (oncall shift).

aly (support): updated CS with list of affected customers + mitigation steps. created webhook to push status updates to customer slack channels for the top 5 customers.

lisa (product): thanks team. please capture timeline + any write-loss risk for postmortem. I'll prepare a customer-facing status blurb once we have confirmation from AWS.

maria (oncall): final note before handoff: current status — degraded (mitigated). 5xx rates reduced to ~15% above baseline. failing targets removed, Route53 weights lowered for 2c, AWS case open. I'll be available on-call for questions during handoff. :white_check_mark:

--- 15 minutes later (continuation) ---

derek (sre): AWS engineer says there's a noisy NIC on a host in us-west-2c causing packet drops on the local fabric, and they're doing host-level remediation and a host replacement. ETA 22 minutes for full remediation.

tim (eng-infra): AWS confirmed problematic hypervisor after tcpdump we uploaded. they offered a recommended action: cordon/reboot host or migrate instances; they performed a replacement and traffic is returning.

incident-bot: automated check 08:43:20Z — ELB unhealthy count returning to normal, Route53 health checks stable.

derek (sre): monitoring now: errors trending back to baseline. I'm going to re-register the healthy instances in 2c one at a time and watch health checks. re-registering yields stable checks for the new host.

aly (support): customer tickets resolved or marked with workaround notes. pushing final inbound message to top 3 affected accounts.

lisa (product): marking customer impact as 'partial, brief' in the internal report draft. request postmortem with timeline + mitigations and a recommendation to add more aggressive Route53 failover for regional health checks.

derek (sre): tentative postmortem tasks: 1) timeline + graphs, 2) why ELB didn't fail faster to other AZs, 3) improve health-check scrubbing to deregister failing hosts sooner, 4) update runbooks for route53 weight shifts.

incident-bot: Incident closed (degraded -> resolved) at 2026-03-15T08:37:47Z. Final notes: AWS host replacement fixed packet loss, customers experienced partial failures for ~25 minutes, no data loss reported. Postmortem requested by product. :memo:

maria (oncall): thanks all. follow-up: schedule postmortem doc and link in this thread when ready. good job on quick mitigation. :beer:
